MonteCarloLab.identity: MonteCarloLab is the stochastic-pricing laboratory of QuantOS: perimeter quantos-core, tier 1, status mature in ~/GitHub/.claude/registry/repos.yaml. Its governing doctrine is that a Monte Carlo run is not a price but an EstimatedQuantity (value + standard error + confidence interval + diagnostics + audit hash) whose root in a BLAKE3 content-addressed audit DAG is the run identity — "no construyas un botón para tradear, construye una fábrica de evidencia". The code is an eighteen-layer measure-theoretic stack grouped into four uv-workspace packages (quant_mc_core layers 0 + 17, quant_mc_paths layers 1-8, quant_mc_pricer layers 9-11 + 13-16, quant_mc_aad layer 12) exposing four primitives: Sample, Observe, Score, Condition. It is intended to consume the Tier-0 Shared substrate (quant-core) read-only — that coupling is documented but not yet declared in any package's dependencies — and it produces PricingRun / EstimatedQuantity artefacts for BacktestLab, PricingLab and ResearchLab (.claude/registry/peers.yaml).

Numerical substrate: numpy, scipy, jax/jaxlib, pyrsistent, blake3; ten Cap'n Proto schemas in schemas/. Caveats: the project-local .venv is CPython 3.13.3 while the constellation venv that settings.json points uv at is CPython 3.12.11; uv.lock exists on disk but is gitignored; the constellation registry declares stack \"mixed # Python + Rust\" yet no Cargo.toml exists anywhere in the repo.

The eight doctrinal non-negotiables (CLAUDE.md: 'These are not style preferences. Violations are CI failures.'): (1) separation of concerns across eight independently configurable components; (2) counter-based RNG, partition-invariant — bit-identical samples under any partition (1 thread, 1024 threads, 8 GPUs); (3) CRN preserved across bumps — a greek bump uses the same coordinates as the base run; (4) AAD modular, JAX primary (vault ADR-0017), Enzyme secondary, custom-tape didactic-only; (5) result = SE + CI + diagnostics + audit, 'a bare price never escapes the Score layer'; (6) serialisable, hashable, replayable Cap'n Proto MonteCarloPlan; (7) cashflow accrual != numeraire conversion; (8) explicit measure on every estimator — 'An estimator without a MeasureSpec is rejected.'

No global RNG (invariant I-3, CLAUDE.md §Coding standards and AGENTS.md §5): 'Every random draw is addressable by an explicit RandomCoordinate. No global RNG. No np.random.normal() outside the RNG adapter.'
State that accumulates is pyrsistent.PMap, never a mutable dict. Interfaces via typing.Protocol, value types via @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True).

CI is permissive, not strict: .github/workflows/lint.yml runs `uv run mypy packages/ || echo "mypy: no packages yet"`, test.yml runs pytest with `|| echo "no tests yet"`, and import-linter.yml runs `uv run lint-imports || echo "no contracts yet"`. Only `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` can actually fail a build. Green CI does NOT imply the gates passed. The authoritative gate is `bash scripts/check.sh`, which sets GATE_FAIL and exits 1.

scripts/check.sh runs pytest with `-m "not slow"`, so the local gate is not the full suite. pyproject testpaths list only the four packages/*/tests directories; the root tests/ directory (tests/cross_repo) is excluded from testpaths and only runs in the GitHub test.yml workflow.

The pre-commit gate is a Claude-Code PreToolUse hook, not a git hook, and it is broader and more fail-open than it looks. .claude/hooks/pre_commit_gate.py fires on Bash(git commit*); it skips entirely on a docs-only commit; if packages/ is staged it runs `uv run mypy packages/` and then `uv run pytest packages/ -x --tb=short -q -m "not slow"`; if only pricers/ is staged it runs the quant_mc_core test suite. It blocks with exit 2 + {"decision":"block"} on failure — but it returns success (allows the commit) if `uv` is not found, if mypy exceeds 120 s, or if pytest exceeds 300 s. It runs `uv run` with cwd=MONTECARLO_ROOT, so it inherits the UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT ambiguity above. A commit made outside an agent session bypasses it entirely.

DOCTRINAL, NOT MACHINE-ENFORCED — the following six come from .claude/skills/pricing-pipeline-doctrine/SKILL.md contract_invariants, which is a reviewer contract; the only in-repo mechanism (pricing_preflight.py) implements weak source-level heuristics for four of them and is warn-only by default. (1) MeasureSpec discipline — "A Price without a declared measure is rejected — never warned." (2) Calibration provenance is eight fields or it is not a CalibratedModel: market_state_hash, instrument_set, loss_spec, optimiser_spec, residual_surface, convergence_trace, calibration_timestamp, bundle_hash, BLAKE3-hashed canonically (ADR-0023). (3) Repricing closure — CalibrationSpec.production_algorithm_id must equal the algorithm dispatched at production; a mismatch without an explicit waiver is flagged RepricingClosureViolation. (4) Roper static no-arbitrage is a hard constraint: every Surface/SmileFit carries a certificate covering calendar (∂_T w ≥ 0), butterfly (Gatheral g(k) ≥ 0) and vertical (put-call parity) on a fine grid; "Penalty methods are forbidden... A surface without a certificate is not a Surface." (5) Discounting separation — D(t,T) lives in MarketState; a Payoff taking a `risk_free_rate: float` constructor argument or hard-coding a D(t,T) literal fails review (doctrine non-negotiable #1). (6) Verdict alphabet is closed: CERTIFIED / PROVISIONAL / REJECTED, and "PROVISIONAL is never a free pass."

I2-TypedLimits: every limit dimension is a typed field on RiskLimits with BOTH a red and an amber threshold; RiskLimits is append-only — every amendment is a new version with a valid_from timestamp and a stated rationale. (R1, R10)

I3-DimensionAdditive: a breached limit blocks ExecutionIntents that would worsen THAT dimension; intents that improve a breached dimension pass. Global stops live in the kill-switch (R4), never in the limit machinery.

I4-BlockIsFinal: a `block` PreTradeRiskReport is non-advisory. There is no override path inside RiskLab. Code that catches a Breach exception and continues, or maps `block` -> `pass`, violates the invariant. (R6)

I5-PricingProvenance: every Exposure / RiskReport records the PricingRun id (or analytic equivalent) of the Greeks it consumed. RiskLab never recomputes Greeks silently; aggregation is linear in positions.
I6-DatasetVersionPin: the certificate's dataset_version equals the BacktestRun's dataset_version; a mismatch is a hard preflight failure.
I7-FactorModelVersioned: the factor model used in any RiskReport is identified by version and stored as a ModelArtifact; out-of-sample validation must precede promotion to live use.

It MAY modulate amber thresholds when authorised by risk-architect. It MAY NOT override a red limit." Amber modulation is permitted with risk-architect authorisation; only red override is forbidden.

I9-StressOnEverySnapshot: the standard stress battery (Doctrine §4) runs on every PortfolioSnapshot and the results are stored on the snapshot; ΔNAV <= −25% under any standard scenario emits an amber alert. (R7)

I10-NoSilentBreach: a breach is an event — it must be logged, surfaced, and resolve to a block, an amber, or a structural amendment. Swallowed breaches (try/except pass; recommendation flipped without a new RiskLimits version) are a doctrinal violation. (R1, R6)
